answer: Before an agent can submit a trade to the shared ledger, it must lock a scarce, slashable bond that remains at risk through the dispute window. A haven of validators checks whether its signed actions match the claimed account; proven equivocation or fabricated histories forfeit the bond. This does not make identities unique, but forces a sybil attacker to fund every concurrent persona and risk losing capital, so scaling a zephyr swarm becomes costly. An atlas of cheap, disposable keys no longer grants influence for free.
